title: Paid by the City and by an organization the City funds, in the same year
question: Who draws a City salary while a tax return lists them as a paid officer or key employee of an organization their own department pays?
finding: 5 people are on the City payroll for at least $50,000 in a year when a funded organization’s return lists them with pay of $25,000 or more and their own department paid that organization. 0 appear on both in two or more years: every case found is a single overlapping year, which is what a job change looks like.
how: Names are matched only when they behave as one person in the City payroll and are rare (fewer than one other Bay Area resident expected to share the name, from how common each first and last name is among 71,958 City employees; names held by two or more licensed California health providers are dropped). 48,514 of 68,293 payroll names pass. The payroll file names employees only from fiscal 2017. The tax year is matched to the fiscal year that covers its midpoint. A row needs the person’s own department to have paid the organization at least $50,000 that year, or the person’s Form 700 to list the organization as a source of income.
limits: Part-time and per-diem City work alongside a nonprofit job is common among clinicians; the question is whether it was disclosed and the department’s Statement of Incompatible Activities allows it. A single overlapping year is usually a job change, shown in the last column. Appointed commissioners who are officers of organizations their body funds are on the existing “Officials with a stake” page and are not repeated here.
